children: Jefferies has stayed away from long-end bonds since July, "as we did not see an easy way out of the U.S.-Iran war," global economist Mohit Kumar says in a note. Positioning is, however, the one factor that is supportive of rates, as it is at stretched levels, according to Jefferies' indicators. "If we do get a weaker [U.S.] CPI print, we could see a knee-jerk short covering of positions going into the Federal Reserve meeting," he says. August CPI data are due on Friday. Analysts in The Wall Street Journal's poll expect the headline index at 3.4%, unchanged from July. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
